title: Why Establishing Classroom Management Is Easier In August
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin's central claim is that teachers get one narrow window — roughly the first three weeks of school — during which establishing real classroom authority is genuinely easy, because students arrive at their most open, attentive, and willing to accept a real leader as they seek a fresh start. He lays out an eight-item first-days checklist: teach the plan in detail, boldly set expectations, model routines precisely, supervise closely, enforce every transgression, reteach sloppy performance, refuse anything less than excellence, and lead students from success to success throughout the day. His warning is that missing this window doesn't just delay progress — it actively lets bad habits and attitudes take root, growing, in his words, "like autumn azaleas." He goes further to argue that most teachers who lose control in this period never successfully restart, not because restarting is impossible, but because fear of aggressive pushback keeps them from taking the stand they should have taken on day one. The piece frames the first few weeks as the single highest-leverage opportunity a teacher gets all year.
points: Students are described as being at their most open and willing to accept real authority in roughly the first three weeks of school.
The eight-item first-days checklist includes teaching the plan in detail, modeling routines precisely, and enforcing every rule transgression.
Missed early expectations don't just stall progress — bad habits are said to take root and grow "like autumn azaleas."
Most teachers who lose control early never successfully restart, largely out of fear of aggressive student pushback.
quotes: The window opens the moment the bell rings on day one and closes less than three weeks later.
Therefore, they’re at their most open, most attentive, and most willing to follow a real-deal leader.
Otherwise, bad behaviors, bad habits, and bad attitudes will grow like autumn azaleas.

The reason is confidence, or lack thereof. The potential for aggressive pushback from students, and even more brazen misbehavior, is so great that they fear taking the stand they should have taken the first day of school.
You have the best opportunity you’re ever going to get to have the teaching experience you really want.
